declared_limits.detail: malformed backend authority 'http://h:80:/x' is rewritten to /x instead of left unchanged; origin-less result, no leak

srs_deltas.note: VE-2 test fr_PROXY_006_AC2_aRemainderThatIsNotARawSuffixIsRefusedBeforeAnyConnection now checks the raw-suffix 400 via Proxy.requestTarget on a real upgrade request; the client sees 101 because FR-PROXY-009 AC-4 hands upgrades to next(). AC-2 wording 'gets 400' should say the guard refuses with 400 at requestTarget level.

A rewritten path a client would read as a network-path (two leading '/' or '\\', tab/CR/LF skipped) gets a leading '/.', e.g. target http://h, Location http://h//evil.example/x -> /.//evil.example/x (keeps 'never place an origin' and avoids open redirect). Implemented and tested.

User information is dropped and an empty port read as omitted before the origin comparison (review FND-001); values whose host/port the Proxy.to grammar refuses (0x port, other schemes, trailing-dot or alternate IPv6 spellings) are treated as other origins and left unchanged.
AC-1, AC-6 and AC-7 already held at base; their tests were green before the implementation commit (DW-1 red-first holds for AC-2..AC-5 only).

out_of_lease_paths.reason: FR-PROXY-009 AC-4/AC-5 (and FR-PROXY-010 AC-1) require WebSocket upgrades to go to next(); the existing FR-PROXY-006 AC-2 test expected the proxy to answer such an upgrade with 400 and hung. It keeps both original checks (requestTarget refuses with 400 on the same decoded request; backend gets 0 requests) and now also asserts the upgrade reaches the app.ws route (101). Recommended option (accept) applied; reviewer confirmed no weakening (FND-003 dropped).
